result.title: Hallucination-Guided Unlearning: Using Hallucination Traces to Reveal Overfitted Memories
result.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: Selective unlearning is increasingly important for the safety and compliance of large language models. Harmful or memorized content is often entangled with useful knowledge and difficult to enumerate. We use the model's own failures to identify candidates for unlearning. We propose Hallucination-Guided Unlearning (HGU), which uses hallucinations as diagnostic signals. HGU localizes unsupported spans via evidence and internal consensus, traces a sparse set of high-responsibility MLP neurons, and edits them with compact gates under a utility-preserving KL constraint. On TOFU, HGU achieves the best MU-FE trade-off, with Avg scores of 0.7221 (forget05) and 0.7699 (forget10), and the highest SepS H-Avg (0.4382/0.4715) under mixed forget/retain prompts. On the WMDP auxiliary task, HGU yields the strongest forgetting (e.g., 14.2 on Economics) while improving Retain (52.7) and MMLU (57.2). These results suggest that tracing hallucinations enables targeted, post-hoc unlearning that better balances forgetting efficacy and general utility without full retraining.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Hallucination-Guided Unlearning（HGU）：把幻觉当作诊断信号，借助证据与内部一致性定位无依据片段，追踪少量高责任 MLP 神经元，并在保效用的 KL 约束下用紧凑门控做后验编辑式选择性遗忘，在 TOFU 与 WMDP 上评估遗忘—效用权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内部共识判定依据支持 + 高责任单元追踪」的归因流程，可能可供核查 LVR 中哪些内部状态真正承载视觉证据、如何做贡献分配与监督；但对象是纯文本遗忘任务，与推理期 latent 状态生成无直接关系，迁移性需阅读原文核实。
